ai.definition: Perplexity Model is a sophisticated language model that leverages advanced machine learning algorithms to produce highly coherent and contextually relevant text.
ai.howItWorks: The model uses deep neural networks, often with architectures like transformers, to process large datasets of textual data. It learns the probability distribution of words in sentences, enabling it to generate text that is not only grammatically correct but also semantically meaningful and contextually appropriate.
ai.problemSolved: Perplexity Model addresses the challenge of generating human-like text that can be used for applications such as chatbots, content generation, and natural language understanding systems where coherence and relevance are critical.
ai.manufacturing: The development process involves training the model on extensive datasets, fine-tuning parameters to optimize performance, and validating its outputs against various metrics.
ai.buildProcess: Training typically requires a large amount of computational power, access to diverse and high-quality data, and iterative refinement through feedback loops involving human evaluators or other models.
ai.costDrivers: High-performance hardware, extensive data storage, energy consumption for training, and the cost of maintaining and updating the model over time are key cost drivers.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The technology is currently in a specification phase, with potential for rapid development as it moves towards early commercialization.
ai.regulation: Regulatory considerations may include data privacy laws, content moderation requirements, and ethical guidelines related to AI usage.
ai.risks: Risks include the potential for bias in training data, security vulnerabilities, and challenges in ensuring model interpretability and transparency.
ai.profitability: Profitability is contingent on successful commercialization, which depends on market demand, competitive landscape, and the ability to integrate the technology into various applications.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development could involve further optimization of the model architecture, integration with other AI technologies, and expansion into new application areas such as creative writing or personalized content generation.

glossary.def: A measure of how difficult it is to predict the next word in a sequence, often used as an evaluation metric for language models.
The degree to which text flows logically and makes sense as a whole.
The extent to which generated text is relevant to the context in which it appears.

subsystems.name: Tokenizer and embedding
subsystems.role: turns raw text into the integer tokens and vectors the network actually computes on.

subsystems.name: Transformer stack
subsystems.role: the core network: billions of parameters that predict the next token.

subsystems.name: Data pipeline
subsystems.role: assembles the training corpus and keeps it clean and legally usable.

subsystems.name: Training infrastructure
subsystems.role: the accelerator cluster that makes months-long training runs possible.
parts: parallelism software (data, tensor and pipeline sharding)

subsystems.name: Post-training stack
subsystems.role: shapes a raw next-token predictor into a helpful, instruction-following assistant.
parts: preference optimisation (RLHF or direct preference methods)

subsystems.name: Serving layer
subsystems.role: runs the trained model cheaply enough to answer real queries.

buildSteps.title: Set the target and the tests
buildSteps.detail: Decide what the model must do — reasoning, coding, retrieval-grounded answers — and build an evaluation harness before training starts, so progress can be measured.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and clean the corpus
buildSteps.detail: Crawl and license text, strip boilerplate, deduplicate near-identical pages, filter low-quality and private material, and tokenise into shards; a modern run consumes hundreds of billions to trillions of tokens.

buildSteps.title: Train the tokenizer
buildSteps.detail: Fit a subword vocabulary of roughly 10^5 entries on a representative sample, balancing short sequences against rare-word coverage.

buildSteps.title: Choose architecture and size
buildSteps.detail: Fix parameter count, context window, and whether to use a sparse mixture of experts so only part of the network runs per token.

buildSteps.title: Pretrain
buildSteps.detail: Run the next-token prediction objective across thousands of accelerators for weeks to months, sharding the model and data across the cluster and checkpointing constantly; compute cost is often measured in the 10^24–10^25 floating-point operations range.

buildSteps.title: Fine-tune on instructions
buildSteps.detail: Train on curated prompt-and-answer demonstrations so the model follows directions rather than merely continuing text.

buildSteps.title: Optimise against preferences
buildSteps.detail: Collect human (and increasingly model-assisted) judgements of which replies are better, and tune the model to prefer them while penalising drift from the base model.

buildSteps.title: Add retrieval, tools and guardrails
buildSteps.detail: Wire in search, document retrieval and calculators so answers can be grounded in sources, and train classifiers that catch unsafe or unsupported output.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate, quantise and serve
buildSteps.detail: Measure intrinsic scores such as perplexity (exponentiated cross-entropy per token) alongside task benchmarks, red-team for harmful behaviour, then compress the weights and deploy behind a batched inference service.

prerequisites.why: the 2017 design that made training on web-scale text practical, and still the basis of every large model.
training needs tens of thousands of chips and the networking to keep them fed with data.
capability scales with the quantity and quality of training text, not just parameter count.

prerequisites.tech: Human preference data and tuning methods
prerequisites.why: this is what turns a text completer into an assistant that answers usefully and safely.
context windows are growing quickly, but attention cost still rises with length and limits very long inputs.
retrieval reduces errors but does not eliminate confident wrong answers, so grounding and citation remain active engineering work.

pathway.milestone: hundreds-of-billions-parameter models served as chat assistants and answer engines, some grounded in live search results
pathway.unlocks: general text, code and summarisation work at low cost per query.

pathway.milestone: sparse mixture-of-experts and long-context models that give frontier quality at lower inference cost
pathway.unlocks: long documents, codebases and multi-document reasoning handled in one pass.

pathway.milestone: agentic tool use, where the model plans, calls tools and checks its own output
pathway.unlocks: multi-step tasks completed end to end rather than single answers.

pathway.milestone: smaller distilled models running on-device with private, always-available assistance
pathway.unlocks: low latency, offline use and lower data-centre energy demand.
